paper.title: Non-Stationary Bandit Learning via Predictive Sampling

settings.name_in_paper: Non-stationary bandit (general reward process, Bayesian framework)
unmapped: Reward process {R_t} is an arbitrary (non-exchangeable) stochastic process evolving exogenously; learner knows its joint distribution (Bayesian prior over the whole process)
Regret measured against the foresight oracle max_a E[R_{t,a} | R_{t+1:inf}] (foresight regret); upper-bounds hindsight regret in reversible bandits
Sub-Gaussianity is of the posterior predictive Pr(R_{t,a} in . | H_{t-1}) almost surely
settings.definition_quote: Let $\mathcal{A}$ be a finite set, and $\{R_t\}_{t = 1}^{+\infty}$ be a stochastic process, where each $R_t = (R_{t,a}: a \in \mathcal{A})$ takes values in $\mathbb{R}^{|\actions|}$. A \emph{bandit} is defined by the tuple $(\{R_t\}_{t = 1}^{+\infty}, \actions)$ ... A bandit is said to be non-stationary if it does not satisfy this property.

unmapped: Each arm's mean is independently redrawn from its initial distribution with known per-arm probability q_a at every step (random switches, not a fixed number S_T)
Learner knows the redraw probabilities q_a and the initial mean distributions
Regret measured against foresight oracle max_a E[R_{t,a} | R_{t+1:inf}]
Each arm's mean is independently redrawn with known probability q_a each step
Regret measured against foresight oracle max_a E[R_{t,a} | R_{t+1:inf}]
settings.definition_quote: There exists a modulated Bernoulli bandit and a constant $C \in \mathbb{R}_{+}$ such that, for all policies $\pi$ and $T \in \mathbb{Z}_{+}$, the foresight regret satisfies ${\mathrm{Regret}}_{\mathrm{F}}(T; \pi) \geq CT$.

symbols.eps_alg: arbitrary epsilon in (0,1) defining the constructed instance

conditions: for a specific constructed Bernoulli (modulated Bernoulli) bandit depending on epsilon
the same instance admits a policy with Return >= (1-epsilon)T

source.label: theorem:performance_difference_1
source.quote: For all $\epsilon \in (0, 1)$, there exists a Bernoulli bandit $\nu$ and a policy $\pi$ such that under $\nu$, $\mathrm{Return}(T; \pi_{\mathrm{TS}}) \leq \epsilon T$, and $\mathrm{Return}(T; \pi) \geq (1 - \epsilon)T$, for all $T \in \mathbb{Z}_{+}$.

results.notes: Negative result for TS: bound is on TS's expected cumulative reward (Return), not regret; it implies regret of TS relative to some policy of at least (1-2eps)T on this instance. Recorded literally as an upper bound on return.

symbols.eps_alg: arbitrary epsilon in (0,1) defining the constructed instance

conditions: on the Bernoulli bandit constructed in the TS negative result (Theorem performance_difference_1)

source.label: theorem:performance_difference_2
source.quote: For all $\epsilon \in (0, 1)$, under the Bernoulli bandit $\nu$ specified in Theorem~\ref{theorem:performance_difference_1}, we have that $\mathrm{Return}(T; \pi_{\mathrm{PS}}) \geq (1-\epsilon) T$, for all $T \in \mathbb{Z}_{+}$.

results.notes: Positive guarantee for PS stated as a lower bound on its expected cumulative reward (return) on one constructed instance; not a regret bound.

symbols.Gamma_sum: sum_{t=1}^T of the information ratio Gamma_t^pi = E[R_{t,bar*} - R_{t,A_t}]^2 / I(R_{t+1:inf}; A_t, R_{t,A_t} | H_{t-1})
symbols.Delta_sum: cumulative predictive information sum_{t=1}^T I(R_{t+1:inf}; R_t | R_{1:t-1})

results.notes: Foresight regret (Bayesian, against oracle seeing future rewards). Holds for any bandit (no sub-Gaussian assumption needed). Upper-bounds hindsight regret for reversible bandits (Proposition strong_regret).

symbols.Delta_sum: cumulative predictive information sum_{t=1}^T I(R_{t+1:inf}; R_t | R_{1:t-1})

conditions: for all t and a, Pr(R_{t,a} in . | H_{t-1}) is almost surely sigma_SG-sub-Gaussian

source.label: th:ps_regret
source.quote: If for all $t \in \mathbb{Z}_+$ and $a \in \actions$, $\Pr(R_{t, a} \in \cdot|H_{t-1})$ is almost surely $\sigma_{\text{SG}}$-sub-Gaussian, then for all $T \in \mathbb{Z}_+$, the regret of PS satisfies ${\mathrm{Regret}}_{\mathrm{F}}(T) \leq \sqrt{2 |\actions| \sigma_{\mathrm{SG}}^2 T \sum_{t = 1}^{T}\Delta_t}$.

results.notes: sigma is the paper's sigma_SG. Foresight regret. In stationary bandits reduces to sqrt(2 K sigma^2 T H(P)), matching Neu et al. (2022) for TS.

symbols.I_S: I(S_2;S_1) + sum_{t=1}^{T-1} I(S_{t+2}; S_{t+1} | S_t) for a hidden Markov state process S_t

conditions: {S_t} is a Markov process such that R_t is independent of all other S's and R's given S_t
for all t and a, Pr(R_{t,a} in . | H_{t-1}) is almost surely sigma_SG-sub-Gaussian

source.label: cor:regret
source.quote: Let $\{S_t\}$ be a Markov process such that ... $R_{t} \perp (S_{1:t-1}, S_{t+1:\infty}, R_{1:t-1}, R_{t+1:\infty}) | S_t$. If for all $t$ and $a$, $\Pr(R_{t, a} \in \cdot|H_{t-1})$ is almost surely $\sigma_{\text{SG}}$-sub-Gaussian, then for all $T$, the regret of PS satisfies ${\mathrm{Regret}}_{\mathrm{F}}(T) \leq \sqrt{2|\actions| \sigma_{\mathrm{SG}}^2 T [\I(S_2;S_1) + \sum_{t = 1}^{T-1} \I(S_{t+2}; S_{t+1} | S_{t})]}$.

results.notes: Foresight regret of PS; refinement of Theorem th:ps_regret via Lemma markov_info.

symbols.I_21: mutual information I(theta_2; theta_1) of the mean-reward vectors
symbols.I_321: conditional mutual information I(theta_3; theta_2 | theta_1)

source.label: theorem:regret_bernoulli
source.quote: In a modulated Bernoulli bandit, for all $T \in \mathbb{Z}_+$, the regret of PS satisfies ${\mathrm{Regret}}_{\mathrm{F}}(T) \leq \sqrt{\frac{1}{2} |\actions| T\left\{ \I(\theta_2; \theta_1) + (T - 1) \I(\theta_3; \theta_2 | \theta_1) \right\}} \leq \sqrt{\frac{1}{2} |\actions| T\left\{ \sum_{a} (1 - q_a) \H(\theta_{1,a}) + (T-1) \sum_{a} \left[2 \H(q_a) + q_a(1 - q_a) \H(\theta_{1,a})\right]\right\}}.

results.notes: First inequality of the theorem. Foresight regret; also bounds hindsight regret since modulated Bernoulli bandits are reversible. Uses sigma_SG = 1/2. Linear in T in general; with q_a = 0 recovers sqrt(K T H(theta_1)/2).

symbols.q_i: redraw probability q_a of arm a
symbols.H_theta_i: entropy H(theta_{1,a}) of arm a's initial mean distribution

results.notes: Second inequality of the same theorem, in terms of per-arm primitives. Entropies in bits (paper's log base 2).

conditions: exists a modulated Bernoulli bandit (two arms, theta_{1,a} ~ unif{0,1}, q = (1/2, 1)) such that the bound holds for all policies and all T

source.label: theorem:lower_bound
source.quote: There exists a modulated Bernoulli bandit and a constant $C \in \mathbb{R}_{+}$ such that, for all policies $\pi$ and $T \in \mathbb{Z}_{+}$, the foresight regret satisfies ${\mathrm{Regret}}_{\mathrm{F}}(T; \pi) \geq CT$.

results.notes: Linear lower bound on foresight regret for a specific instance; constant C = 1/272 from the proof. Renamed C to C_lb to avoid clash with corruption budget.
